subject.title: Matrix DM session-key lowercasing collides case-distinct MXIDs, sharing one peer's DM transcript with another under per-peer scope

question: Should OpenClaw reverse the prior Matrix-DM-out-of-scope behavior and enroll opaque direct peer IDs, including Matrix and possibly Signal, in case-preserving session-key construction?
rationale: The existing docs promise DM isolation, but changing direct-key case behavior affects security, legacy lowercased rows, and a prior maintainer-merged scope decision from the Matrix room-id fix.

options.title: Sponsor narrow security fix
options.body: Preserve Matrix direct MXID case under non-main dmScope, add legacy alias proof/migration safeguards, and include Signal direct only after direct-ID contract proof.

options.title: Matrix-only first
options.body: Fix Matrix direct MXIDs now and leave Signal direct out until a separate issue proves Signal direct IDs are case-sensitive principals.

options.title: Keep current lowercase behavior
options.body: Document that Matrix per-user DM isolation is unsafe for case-distinct MXIDs and require Matrix per-room scoping or separate gateways for that deployment class.

recommendation.title: Sponsor narrow security fix
recommendation.body: Preserve Matrix direct MXID case under non-main dmScope, add legacy alias proof/migration safeguards, and include Signal direct only after direct-ID contract proof.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged and carried the prior Matrix opaque-ID case-preservation work and its alias-safety fixups.
